```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr); library(readr); library(tidyr); library(purrr); library(stringr); library(ggplot2); library(knitr)
})
# `params` only exists when knitting. Fall back to defaults when chunks are run
# interactively (Run All), so the file works either way.
if (!exists("params")) {
  params <- list(data = "data/players.csv", results_dir = "results", season_z = TRUE)
}
dir.create(params$results_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Goal

Predict whether a college player is taken in the **first round** from his final
college season (plus simple multi-season features). This is the baseline the
other four models (KNN, ANN, random forest, XGBoost) are compared against.

Evaluation is **leave-one-draft-out**: train on every other draft class, predict
the held-out class. Never random row splits — players from the same class leak.

## Data

```{r load}
df <- read_csv(params$data, show_col_types = FALSE)

# Core feature set agreed by the team (see data/data_dictionary.csv for definitions).
# Dummies / flags listed in `binary_features` are not z-scored.
features <- c(
  # profile
  "class_num",            # Fr=1 ... Sr=4 (age proxy; younger = more valuable)
  "height_vs_pos",        # height relative to position average (swap for "height_in" to compare)
  "pos_wing", "pos_big",  # position dummies, guard = reference
  "recruit_rank", "unranked",
  "transfer",
  # role / load
  "mpg", "usg",
  # efficiency and shooting
  "TS_per", "FT_per", "TPA_rate", "TP_per_shrunk", "ftr", "pts_per40",
  # playmaking / rebounding / defense
  "ast_tov", "ORB_per", "DRB_per", "stl_per", "blk_per",
  # all-in-one impact
  "obpm", "dbpm",
  # competition level
  "team_adj_em"
)
binary_features <- c("pos_wing", "pos_big", "unranked", "transfer", "power_conf")
features <- intersect(features, names(df))

cat("Rows:", nrow(df), "  first-rounders:", sum(df$first_round),
    "  drafts:", n_distinct(df$draft_year), "\n")
df |> count(draft_year, first_round) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = first_round, values_from = n, names_prefix = "fr_") |>
  kable(caption = "Rows per draft year (fr_1 = first-rounders)")
```

## Preprocessing

Missing values: median-impute and add a `_missing` flag. Then z-score each stat
**within its draft year** so the model isn't confused by era shifts in pace and
3-point volume.

```{r preprocess}
flag_cols <- character()
for (f in features) {
  if (anyNA(df[[f]])) {
    flag <- paste0(f, "_missing")
    df[[flag]] <- as.integer(is.na(df[[f]]))
    df[[f]]    <- ifelse(is.na(df[[f]]), median(df[[f]], na.rm = TRUE), df[[f]])
    flag_cols  <- c(flag_cols, flag)
  }
}

# Stats that mostly reflect position (a center blocks 5x more shots than a guard).
# These are standardized within position x season, so they read "good at this
# FOR YOUR POSITION". Everything else is standardized within season only.
pos_relative_features <- c("blk_per", "stl_per", "ORB_per", "DRB_per", "treb_per40",
                           "AST_per", "ast_tov", "ast_per40", "TPA_rate", "TP_per_shrunk",
                           "TPA_per40", "rim_rate", "dunks_per40", "height_in")
zs <- function(x) { s <- sd(x, na.rm = TRUE); if (is.na(s) || s == 0) 0 * x else (x - mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)) / s }

if (params$season_z) {
  z_feats   <- setdiff(features, binary_features)
  z_pos     <- intersect(z_feats, pos_relative_features)
  z_season  <- setdiff(z_feats, z_pos)
  df <- df |> mutate(position = ifelse(is.na(position), "unknown", position))
  df <- df |> group_by(draft_year) |> mutate(across(all_of(z_season), zs)) |> ungroup()
  if (length(z_pos))
    df <- df |> group_by(draft_year, position) |> mutate(across(all_of(z_pos), zs)) |> ungroup()
  cat("Standardized within position x season:", paste(z_pos, collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
x_cols <- c(features, flag_cols)
# Drop anything constant (glm would return NA for it)
const <- x_cols[sapply(df[x_cols], function(v) sd(v, na.rm = TRUE) == 0 | all(is.na(v)))]
if (length(const)) { cat("Dropping constant features:", paste(const, collapse = ", "), "\n"); x_cols <- setdiff(x_cols, const) }
cat("Features:", paste(x_cols, collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

## Helper: metrics

```{r metrics}
pr_auc <- function(y, p) {           # average precision
  o <- order(-p); y <- y[o]
  tp <- cumsum(y); prec <- tp / seq_along(y)
  sum(prec * y) / max(sum(y), 1)
}
roc_auc <- function(y, p) {
  if (length(unique(y)) < 2) return(NA_real_)
  r <- rank(p); n1 <- sum(y == 1); n0 <- sum(y == 0)
  (sum(r[y == 1]) - n1 * (n1 + 1) / 2) / (n1 * n0)
}
log_loss <- function(y, p, eps = 1e-15) {
  p <- pmin(pmax(p, eps), 1 - eps); -mean(y * log(p) + (1 - y) * log(1 - p))
}
```

## Leave-one-draft-out logistic regression

Class imbalance is handled with weights (positives up-weighted so both classes
sum to the same total). The model is plain `glm`; regularized alternatives
(`glmnet`) are a natural next step.

```{r model-functions}
fit_weighted_glm <- function(train, x_cols) {
  y <- train$first_round
  w <- ifelse(y == 1, 0.5 / mean(y == 1), 0.5 / mean(y == 0))   # "balanced" weights
  form <- as.formula(paste("first_round ~", paste(x_cols, collapse = " + ")))
  suppressWarnings(glm(form, data = train, family = binomial(), weights = w))
}

# Leave-one-draft-out: returns per-year metrics and out-of-sample predictions
run_lodo <- function(df, x_cols) {
  preds <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(df)); per_year <- list()
  for (yr in sort(unique(df$draft_year))) {
    tr <- df |> filter(draft_year != yr); te_idx <- which(df$draft_year == yr)
    mu <- sapply(tr[x_cols], mean); sdv <- sapply(tr[x_cols], sd); sdv[sdv == 0 | is.na(sdv)] <- 1
    scale_df <- function(d) { d[x_cols] <- sweep(sweep(d[x_cols], 2, mu), 2, sdv, "/"); d }
    m <- fit_weighted_glm(scale_df(tr), x_cols)
    p <- predict(m, newdata = scale_df(df[te_idx, ]), type = "response")
    preds[te_idx] <- p
    y <- df$first_round[te_idx]; n_fr <- sum(y)
    if (n_fr == 0) next
    hits <- sum(y[order(-p)][seq_len(n_fr)])
    per_year[[as.character(yr)]] <- tibble(
      draft_year = yr, n_rows = length(te_idx), n_first_round = n_fr,
      pr_auc = pr_auc(y, p), roc_auc = roc_auc(y, p), log_loss = log_loss(y, p),
      top_n_hits = hits, top_n_precision = hits / n_fr)
  }
  list(per_year = bind_rows(per_year), preds = preds)
}

# Standardized coefficients from a fit on all years
full_coefs <- function(df, x_cols) {
  mu <- sapply(df[x_cols], mean); sdv <- sapply(df[x_cols], sd); sdv[sdv == 0 | is.na(sdv)] <- 1
  d <- df; d[x_cols] <- sweep(sweep(d[x_cols], 2, mu), 2, sdv, "/")
  m <- fit_weighted_glm(d, x_cols)
  tibble(feature = names(coef(m)), coef = coef(m)) |> filter(feature != "(Intercept)", !is.na(coef)) |>
    arrange(desc(coef))
}

overall_table <- function(df, res) {
  y <- df$first_round; p <- res$preds
  tibble(metric = c("PR-AUC", "baseline PR-AUC (positive rate)", "ROC-AUC", "log loss", "top-n precision (mean over drafts)"),
         value  = c(pr_auc(y, p), mean(y), roc_auc(y, p), log_loss(y, p), mean(res$per_year$top_n_precision)))
}
```

### Pass 1: all features

```{r pass1}
res1   <- run_lodo(df, x_cols)
coefs1 <- full_coefs(df, x_cols)
kable(overall_table(df, res1), digits = 3, caption = "Pass 1 — overall")
kable(coefs1, digits = 3, caption = "Pass 1 — standardized coefficients")
```

### Pass 2: drop the 3 weakest features

Backward elimination, one step: remove the three features with the smallest
absolute standardized coefficient (missing-value flags are not candidates), refit.
This is the final model.

```{r pass2}
n_drop <- 3
candidates <- coefs1 |> filter(!str_detect(feature, "_missing$")) |> arrange(abs(coef))
dropped <- head(candidates$feature, n_drop)
cat("Dropped:", paste(sprintf("%s (%.3f)", dropped, candidates$coef[seq_len(n_drop)]), collapse = ", "), "\n")

x_final <- setdiff(x_cols, dropped)
res   <- run_lodo(df, x_final)
coefs <- full_coefs(df, x_final)
per_year <- res$per_year
df$p_first_round <- res$preds

kable(per_year, digits = 3, caption = "Final model — per-draft results (leave-one-draft-out)")
kable(overall_table(df, res), digits = 3, caption = "Final model — overall")
```

### Position check: is the model over-picking bigs?

For each draft class, take the model's top-n (n = number of real first-rounders
that year) and compare its position mix with the real first round. If the
"model top-n" share for bigs is well above the "actual" share, the model is
over-paying for size.

```{r position-check}
pos_check <- df |> group_by(draft_year) |>
  mutate(n_fr = sum(first_round), in_model_topn = rank(-p_first_round, ties.method = "first") <= n_fr) |>
  ungroup() |>
  group_by(position) |>
  summarise(pool_share       = n() / nrow(df),
            actual_1st_round = sum(first_round),
            model_topn       = sum(in_model_topn),
            hits_in_topn     = sum(in_model_topn & first_round == 1), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(actual_share = actual_1st_round / sum(actual_1st_round),
         model_share  = model_topn / sum(model_topn),
         precision    = hits_in_topn / model_topn) |>
  select(position, pool_share, actual_1st_round, actual_share, model_topn, model_share, precision)
kable(pos_check, digits = 3, caption = "Position mix: pool vs. actual first round vs. model's top-n")
```

```{r plot-per-year, fig.height=3.5}
ggplot(per_year, aes(draft_year, top_n_precision)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") + ylim(0, 1) +
  labs(title = "Share of real first-rounders found in the model's top-n, by draft",
       x = NULL, y = "top-n precision") + theme_minimal()
```

## Coefficients (final model)

Signs to check: `class_num` and `recruit_rank` negative (younger / higher-ranked
recruits = more valuable), `obpm`, `height_vs_pos`, `usg` positive. If they're
wrong, it's almost always a join problem — look at `match_report.txt` first.

Remember these are *conditional* effects: a negative coefficient on, say,
`ORB_per` means "given height and position, extra offensive rebounding doesn't
add first-round value", not that rebounding is bad.

On height: the model uses `height_vs_pos` (height relative to the position
average) rather than raw height, so "tall" means tall *for a guard* or tall
*for a big*. If height still dominates, check the "Non-first-rounders the model
liked most" table below: if it's full of 7-footers with weak stats, the model is
over-paying for size and a position × height interaction or a cap is the next step.

```{r coef}
kable(coefs, digits = 3, caption = "Standardized coefficients (+ = more likely first round)")

ggplot(coefs, aes(reorder(feature, coef), coef, fill = coef > 0)) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) + coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "coefficient", title = "Logistic regression coefficients (final model)") + theme_minimal()
```

## Biggest disagreements with the draft

```{r misses}
df <- df |> group_by(draft_year) |>
  mutate(rank_in_class = rank(-p_first_round, ties.method = "first")) |> ungroup()
df <- df |> mutate(pick = ifelse(is.na(pick_number), "Undrafted", as.character(pick_number)))
show <- c("draft_year", "player_name", "school", "position", "ht", "class_year", "pick", "p_first_round", "rank_in_class")
show <- intersect(show, names(df))

df |> filter(first_round == 1) |> arrange(p_first_round) |> head(15) |> select(all_of(show)) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "First-rounders the model liked least")
df |> filter(first_round == 0) |> arrange(desc(p_first_round)) |> head(15) |> select(all_of(show)) |>
  kable(digits = 3, caption = "Non-first-rounders the model liked most")
```

## Save results

```{r save}
write_csv(per_year, file.path(params$results_dir, "logreg_per_year.csv"))
write_csv(coefs,    file.path(params$results_dir, "logreg_coefficients.csv"))
df |> mutate(pick_number = ifelse(is.na(pick_number), "Undrafted", as.character(pick_number))) |>
  select(pid, player_name, school, position, ht, draft_year, class_year, first_round, pick_number, p_first_round, rank_in_class) |>
  write_csv(file.path(params$results_dir, "logreg_predictions.csv"))
```

## For the other four models

Reuse this exact loop: same `players.csv`, same leave-one-draft-out split, same
metrics. Swap `fit_weighted_glm` for `class::knn`, `nnet::nnet`,
`randomForest::randomForest`, or `xgboost::xgboost`. KNN and the ANN need the
scaling; the tree models don't (and xgboost takes NAs directly, so the
imputation step can be skipped for it).
